messages.subject: expected.test() in twodimensional model
parts:
hi phil,

i have a model with 2 (highly) correlated factors, each made up of a distinct set of items (different questionnaires):

mod =   "F1 = 1-9
         F2 = 10-21
         COV = F1*F2"

i want to estimate the expected scores from the item set constituting factor 1 solely by the theta of factor 2. i tried to do so with the EAPsum method, but it requires a full dataset without NAs, so i cannot simply set all the factor 1 items to NA in my data. my second thought was to refit the model to a dataset containing only the needed items, but i cannot think of a way to reformulate the twodimensional model without the items of factor 1.

i guess  i can use spline regression or something to establish an empirical relation, but i wonder whether you have an idea how to achieve a model based?

thanks a lot, felix

parts:
On Fri, May 15, 2015 at 2:22 PM, Dr. Hans Hansen <bea...@gmx.de> wrote:

hi phil,

i have a model with 2 (highly) correlated factors, each made up of a distinct set of items (different questionnaires):

mod =   "F1 = 1-9
         F2 = 10-21
         COV = F1*F2"

i want to estimate the expected scores from the item set constituting factor 1 solely by the theta of factor 2.
For what purpose? The covariance/correlation you get from the above model essentially answers this question.

i tried to do so with the EAPsum method, but it requires a full dataset without NAs, so i cannot simply set all the factor 1 items to NA in my data. my second thought was to refit the model to a dataset containing only the needed items, but i cannot think of a way to reformulate the twodimensional model without the items of factor 1.

i guess  i can use spline regression or something to establish an empirical relation, but i wonder whether you have an idea how to achieve a model based?

If you are looking for how one test could predict another at a different time (meaning that the testing times are essentially independent) then you would probably want to fit two separate unidimensional models, using the plausible.draws input to fscores(), and determine the relationship by averaging over the sets of values.  You could do a similar thing using point estimates like EAP or MAP, but these are subject to shrinkage effects (but may be more in line with what you are after). HTH, cheers.

Phil

thanks a lot, felix
